questions.title: Send Method Purpose
questions.description: What does Ruby's `send` method do?
questions.Option1: It sends an HTTP request to a remote URL
questions.Option2: It invokes a method on an object by name (string or symbol), passing arguments
questions.Option4: It returns the class of an object

questions.title: Define Method Purpose
questions.description: What does `define_method` do in Ruby?
questions.Option2: It dynamically creates an instance method on a class using a block as the method body

questions.title: Method Missing Trigger
questions.description: When is `method_missing` invoked?
questions.Option1: Whenever any method is called on any object
questions.Option2: When a method that is not defined is called on an object
questions.Option3: When a class is being defined

questions.title: Class Eval Context
questions.description: In what context does `class_eval` run its block?
questions.Option1: In the context of a class (self is the class)
questions.Option2: In the context of an instance of an object
questions.Option3: In the context of the top-level main object
questions.Option4: In the context of the Kernel module

questions.title: Respond To Return Value
questions.description: What does `obj.respond_to?(:foo)` return?
questions.Option2: true if obj has a method foo, false otherwise

questions.title: Instance Eval Context
questions.description: In what context does `instance_eval` run its block?
questions.Option1: In the context of a class
questions.Option2: In the context of a specific object instance (self is that instance)
questions.Option3: In the context of the Kernel module
questions.Option4: In the context of a thread

questions.title: Send Symbol Output
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class A
  def m; "hello"; end
end
puts A.new.send(:m)

questions.title: Define Method Then Call
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class B
  define_method(:greet) { "Hi" }
end
puts B.new.greet

questions.title: Method Missing Handles Foo
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class C
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    "missing:#{name}"
  end
end
puts C.new.foo

questions.title: Respond To On Missing Method
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class R
  def foo; end
end
r = R.new
puts r.respond_to?(:bar)

questions.title: Send Bypasses Private Visibility
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class S
  def visible; "pub"; end
  private
  def hidden; "priv"; end
end
s = S.new
puts s.send(:hidden)

questions.title: Define Method Closure Capture
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class D
  [:a, :b, :c].each_with_index do |m, i|
    define_method(m) { i + 1 }
  end
end
d = D.new
puts d.a, d.b, d.c

questions.title: Method Missing Returns Sum
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class M
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    args.sum
  end
end
puts M.new.calculate(1, 2, 3, 4)

questions.title: Class Eval Adds Method
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class E; end
E.class_eval do
  def hi; "hi"; end
end
puts E.new.hi

questions.title: Respond To False For Undefined
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class R
  def foo; "foo"; end

questions.title: Why Override Respond To With Missing
questions.description: Why should you override `respond_to?` when overriding `method_missing`?
questions.Option2: To keep respond_to? consistent with the dynamic methods method_missing handles
questions.Option3: To prevent other classes from inheriting
questions.Option4: It is mandatory or Ruby raises an error

questions.title: Send Calls Private Method
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class A
  private
  def secret; 42; end
end
puts A.new.send(:secret)

questions.title: Method Missing Super Fallback
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class B
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    return "handled:#{name}" if name.to_s.start_with?("do_")
    super
  end
end
begin
  B.new.do_thing
  B.new.other
rescue NoMethodError
  puts "caught"
end

questions.title: Define Method Inside Class Eval
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class Q; end
[:x, :y].each do |m|
  Q.class_eval { define_method(m) { m.to_s } }
end
puts Q.new.x, Q.new.y

questions.title: Respond To And Missing Combined
questions.description: What does this Ruby code print?
questions.codesnippet:
class O
  def respond_to?(name)
    name.to_s.start_with?("dyn_") ? true : super
  end
  def method_missing(name, *args)
    name.to_s.start_with?("dyn_") ? "dynamic:#{name}" : super
  end
end
o = O.new
puts o.respond_to?(:dyn_a)
puts o.dyn_a
puts o.respond_to?(:foo)
